title: Backtracking
short: Try every choice, undo it, and try the next one.
what: Some problems ask for all the ways to do something: every subset, every order, every valid board. Backtracking builds an answer one choice at a time. When it reaches the end, or a dead end, it undoes the last choice and tries the next option. It's recursion with an undo step.
analogy: Walking a maze with a rule: at each fork take the first path, and when you hit a wall, walk back to the last fork and take the next path.

frames.label: subsets of [1, 2, 3]
frames.say: List every subset of [1, 2, 3]. At each number you choose: take it or skip it. Start with an empty path [].

frames.label: go deep
frames.say: Go down the left side: take 1, take 2, take 3. No numbers left, so record the path [1, 2, 3].

frames.label: undo, try other
frames.say: Step back: undo the 3 (pop it from the path) and try the other option, skip 3. Record [1, 2]. That undo is the backtrack.

frames.label: back up two
frames.say: Both options under [1, 2] are done, so back up to [1] and skip 2. Taking or skipping 3 gives [1, 3] and [1].

frames.label: other half
frames.say: Back at the start, skip 1 and run the same pattern again: [2, 3], [2], [3], [].

frames.label: all leaves
frames.say: 8 leaves, 8 subsets: 2 options for each of 3 numbers is 2 x 2 x 2. If a branch can't work, stop early and skip its whole subtree.

when: Find all subsets, permutations or combinations
Find every path or word that fits
The input is small (about 20 items or fewer)
python:
def subsets(nums):
    out, path = [], []
    def go(i):
        if i == len(nums):
            out.append(path[:])  # copy, the path keeps changing
            return
        path.append(nums[i])     # choose: take nums[i]
        go(i + 1)
        path.pop()               # undo the choice
        go(i + 1)                # other option: skip nums[i]
    go(0)
    return out
print(subsets([1, 2, 3]))
watch: Save a copy of the path (path[:]), not the path itself, or every answer ends up empty.
Every choice needs a matching undo right after the recursive call.
Prune: stop a branch as soon as it can't lead to a valid answer.
